Austin Tyler Reaves was born on May 29, 1998.
Austin Reaves is an American professional basketball player.
Austin Reaves plays for the Los Angeles Lakers of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Reaves played college basketball for the Wichita State Shockers and the Oklahoma Sooners.
Reaves joined the Lakers as an undrafted free agent.
Reaves attended Cedar Ridge High School in Newark, Arkansas.
Reaves won back-to-back Class 2A state titles during his first two years of high school.
Reaves scored 73 points in a triple-overtime win over Forrest City High School.
As a senior at Cedar Ridge High School, Reaves averaged 32.5 points, 8.8 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game.
Reaves led his team to a Class 3A state title as a senior.
Reaves was named MVP of the state tournament after averaging 43.3 points through four games during his senior year.
Reaves was a two-time Class 3A All-State selection.
On January 20, 2016, Reaves committed to playing college basketball for Wichita State over offers from South Dakota State and Arkansas State.
During his freshman season at Wichita State, Reaves underwent surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder.
Reaves had been playing through the injury since his junior year of high school.
As a freshman at Wichita State, Reaves averaged 4.1 points per game in a reserve role.
After the season, Reaves underwent surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder, which had dislocated three times during his college career and caused him to miss games.
On January 28, 2018, Reaves posted a sophomore season-high 23 points and four assists in a 90–71 win over Tulsa.
Reaves made seven three-pointers in the first half of that game, setting a program record for most three-pointers in a half.
As a sophomore at Wichita State, Reaves averaged 8.1 points and 3.1 rebounds per game, shooting 42.5 percent from three-point range.
After his sophomore season, Reaves transferred to Oklahoma and sat out the following season due to NCAA transfer rules.
During his redshirt year, Reaves weight trained and gained 20 pounds (9 kg).
On March 7, 2020, Reaves recorded a career-high 41 points, six assists and five rebounds in a 78–76 win over TCU.
Reaves led a 19-point second-half comeback and made the game-winning shot with 0.5 seconds remaining in that game.
As a redshirt junior at Oklahoma, Reaves averaged 14.7 points, 5.3 rebounds and three assists per game and was named to the Big 12 All-Newcomer Team.
On December 6, 2020, Reaves posted a senior season-high 32 points, nine assists and six rebounds in an 82–78 win against TCU.
In the second round of the NCAA tournament, Reaves scored 27 points in an 87–71 loss to top-seeded Gonzaga.
As a senior at Oklahoma, Reaves averaged 18.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game, earning First Team All-Big 12 honors.
On March 31, 2021, Reaves declared for the 2021 NBA draft, forgoing his remaining college eligibility.
Reaves went undrafted in the 2021 NBA draft after declining to be selected 42nd overall by the Detroit Pistons.
On August 3, 2021, Reaves signed a two-way contract with the Los Angeles Lakers.
On September 27, 2021, Reaves was signed to a standard NBA contract.
On October 22, 2021, Reaves made his NBA debut, scoring eight points off the bench in a 115–105 loss to the Phoenix Suns.
On December 15, 2021, Reaves scored 15 points, on 5-of-6 shooting from three, grabbed 7 rebounds, and hit a game-winning 3-pointer in a 107–104 victory over the Dallas Mavericks.
During the Lakers' season finale on April 10, 2022, Reaves notched the first triple-double of his career with 16 rebounds and 10 assists along with 31 points in 42 minutes.
On March 19, 2023, Reaves scored a career-high 35 points with six rebounds and six assists off the bench in a 111–105 win against the Orlando Magic.
On April 16, 2023, Reaves scored 23 points in game 1 of the first-round playoff series against the Memphis Grizzlies.
Reaves matched that performance in game 4 of the same series, leading the Lakers in scoring with a 117–111 overtime victory.
Reaves' successful rookie year led to him receiving nicknames "Hillbilly Kobe", "White Kobe", and "AR-15".
On July 6, 2023, Reaves re-signed with the Los Angeles Lakers on a four-year, $54 million contract.
Reaves started the first eight games of the 2023–24 season for a streak of 34 consecutive starts dating back to the 2022–23 regular season and playoffs.
On December 9, 2023, Reaves and the Lakers won the inaugural season of the NBA In-Season Tournament.
Reaves scored 28 points off the bench in the championship game against Indiana.
On January 31, 2024, Reaves put up a then-season-high 28 points along with six assists and two steals in a 138–122 loss to the Atlanta Hawks.
In his next game on February 1, 2024, Reaves put up 32 points on a career-high seven three-pointers made in a 114–105 win over the Boston Celtics.
On February 3, 2024, Reaves provided 22 points, six rebounds, seven assists, and two blocks as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the New York Knicks 113-105.
Playing without LeBron James on March 26 against the Milwaukee Bucks, Reaves had a triple-double with 29 points, 14 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 128–124 road win in double overtime.
Reaves was selected to play on the 2023 U.S. national team for the FIBA World Cup.
Reaves is the son of Nicole Wilkett and Brian Reaves.
Both of his parents played college basketball for Arkansas State.
His mother, Nicole Wilkett, averaged 21.3 points per game and earned all-conference honors as a senior at Arkansas State.
His father, Brian Reaves, tied for third in program history with 384 career assists.
Reaves' brother, Spencer, played college basketball for North Greenville and Central Missouri before embarking on a professional career with Juaristi ISB in Spain.
As of 2023–24, Spencer is with Rasta Vechta in Germany.
Reaves credits his brother for sparking his interest in basketball.
Reaves' grandmother is German, which allowed him to obtain a German passport in 2022.
In 2023, Reaves expressed interest in playing for Germany's national team but later joined the 2023 U.S. World Cup team.
In March 2023, Reaves signed a signature shoe deal with Chinese sports apparel brand Rigorer.
The first shoe named "AR1" was released in August 2023 via sneaker marketplace Kicks Crew.
